detail: 'Establish registration of new vehicle', customer type Private. Includes light commercials (no body-type field).

'Registration New', customer Individual, year of manufacture within one year. QLD file covers passenger body types only, so NSW and QLD levels are not directly comparable — compare gradients within each state.
NSW: EV / BATTERY ELECTRIC / ELECTRICITY. QLD: Electric. VIC: fuel code E. PHEV only separable in NSW.
Passenger, off-road, forward-control passenger and light goods vehicles; quarter-end snapshots.
Distinct BEVs seen in any QLD transaction since Jan 2022 at their last known LGA; per 1,000 earners.
Vehicle class 2 (excludes motorcycles). Recent-model = year of manufacture >= snapshot year - 1.
Earner-weighted quintiles within each state. Q1 = lowest median income.
Areas ranked on the metric named; only areas above the minimum-size thresholds on Inputs are ranked, so tiny areas don't top the lists on noise.
Shows where BEVs are registered, not the buyer's income. Retiree and student areas have low median taxable income but not necessarily low wealth.
FBT-exempt EV novated leases (since Jul 2022) are usually registered to the employee, so they count as private and favour salaried areas.
LGA income 2022-23, postcode income 2023-24; registrations 2023–2026. Area income rankings move slowly.
QLD LGAs are large (Brisbane ~ a quarter of earners), so QLD income groups are lumpy.
No state publishes EV registrations by suburb. The finest public geography is postcode (VIC) and LGA (NSW, QLD); the 'top 10' tables use those.

The crisis comparison is before/after: other 2026 changes (new cheaper BEV models, NVES penalties, incentives) also act on the same months. The same-months-a-year-earlier baseline removes seasonality, not those.

Some NSW months in 2023–24 have a block of rows with no make or fuel (TfNSW 'Other/Unmapped'); these are excluded, so counts in those months are low. Shares are unaffected if the block is spread across fuels.
